description: The team is composed of two university students — one majoring in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, and the other in Accounting. Together, they bring a dynamic blend of technical and analytical skills, united by a shared passion for developing innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Leveraging their diverse expertise, they collaborated to create EG FireTrack - website that harmonizes NASA MODIS + VIIRS fire hotspots for Borneo.
summary: We developed EG FireTrack, a live web dashboard that turns 10 years (2017–2026) of NASA satellite fire data into one consistent wildfire record and early-warning system for the island of Borneo. The website is built for fire managers, emergency responders, land managers and scientists. NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS sensors detect fires differently. MODIS pixels are much larger, while VIIRS pixels are about seven times smaller in area. So raw counts are inconsistent and often double-counted. EG FireTrack harmonizes both onto a common 1 km grid, counting a fire once when detections match within ±1 km and ±1 hour, and calibrating MODIS to the VIIRS scale. This produces a validated record that is updated daily from NASA FIRMS. The website analyses where and when fires happen and how today compares with normal, forecasts the 72-hour chance of spreading with machine learning, predicts the next three months, and suggests alert levels, rescue priority and actions through a transparent 0–100 risk score. This matters because Borneo’s peatland fires cause transboundary haze that harms health and ecosystems. Consistent data and explainable warnings help agencies act earlier and send resources where they are needed most.
details:
Problem Statement

Every year, forest and peatland fires burn across the island of Borneo. The fires destroy forests and wildlife habitat and release large amounts of carbon. They also create transboundary haze, which closes schools, harms public health, and drifts into neighbouring countries. Peat fires are especially dangerous because they can burn underground for weeks.

NASA satellites detect these fires every day, but its two main fire sensors count them differently. MODIS uses 1 km pixels while VIIRS uses 375 m pixels, about seven times smaller in area. One fire can appear as several VIIRS hotspots but only one MODIS hotspot. So raw counts are inconsistent, double-counted, and hard to compare across years. Fire agencies also receive dots on a map rather than clear answers: Is today unusual? Which fire is most dangerous? Who should respond, and with what? There is a critical need for a system that harmonizes NASA’s fire data into one reliable record and turns it into timely, explainable action.

Vision, Mission, and Objectives

Vision: A Borneo where every wildfire is detected early, understood clearly and answered quickly, powered by NASA Earth observation and transparent decision support.

Mission: To harmonize NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS fire observations into one consistent record, and to transform it into forecasts, alert levels and response recommendations that help agencies protect people and ecosystems.

Objectives:

  • Build a harmonized 10-year fire record (2017–2026) that counts fires consistently across MODIS and VIIRS.
  • Show where and when fires happen, and whether today is normal or unusual.
  • Forecast the 72-hour chance of fire spreading and the next 3 months of activity, with understandable reasons.
  • Convert forecasts into clear alert levels, rescue priority and recommended actions for the responsible agency.
  • Keep the system live, automatic and free to access through one link.

Considerations

  • Selection of NASA fire datasets (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m) that fully cover the 10-year window, with the record continuing on NOAA-20 after S-NPP ended.
  • Fair harmonization and comparison for a common 1 km grid, no double counting, and a median “normal” baseline with a minimum floor.
  • Designing an intuitive interface with clear color-coded alert levels and visual maps, calendars, and charts.
  • Balancing machine-learning accuracy with explainability and safety, so forecasts show their reasons and the agency in charge makes the final decision.
  • Maintaining reliability and scalability for daily automatic updates at no cost, a protected API key, and easy extension to other fire-prone regions.

Project Details Overview

Our Github Link: Github

Our User Guide Video Link:


EG FireTrack is an interactive web-based dashboard that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS active fire data into one consistent 10-year wildfire record (2017–2026) for Borneo. It turns it into early warnings and response guidance. The platform is built on five main features:

  • Harmonized: MODIS and VIIRS merged into one record on a common 1 km grid, with every fire counted once.
  • Analysis: where and when fires happen, and how today compares with normal (the 2017–2025 median).
  • Forecast: a machine-learning (LightGBM) estimate of the chance a fire spreads in the next 72 hours, with clear reasons.
  • Prediction: expected hotspots and fire intensity for the next 3 months, with a likely range.
  • Suggestion: a 0–100 Risk Score that sets the alert level (Low, Moderate, High or Critical), rescue priority and recommended actions.
The Risk Score is computed with a weighted formula: chance of spreading (40 points), compared to normal (20), people exposed (15), fire intensity and growth (10), peat fuel (10) and cross-border haze (5).

It draws on NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m active fires), together with GADM boundaries and Open-Meteo weather. These let fire managers, emergency responders and scientists understand the situation and act on it quickly. The system updates itself every day from NASA FIRMS.

About EG FireTrack

  • Map view (Main Portal) shows where the fires are: hotspot dots sized by fire intensity, summaries for Borneo and the selected area, and the top 5 districts.
  • Calendar view shows when fires happen: a 10-year × 12-month heatmap, yearly totals, and the fire season.
  • Analysis view shows the trend from past to now: the next 3 months for MODIS, VIIRS, and the harmonized record, plus the rescue risk status and the harmonization check.
  • Alerts and Response show what to do and where first: alert levels, situation reports, reasons, recommended actions, resources, coordination, rescue priority, and a “Notify nearby teams” button.
  • A data status indicator showing data freshness, CSV download, and a full PDF report.

Technical Skills and Tools

  • Python (pandas, GeoPandas, DuckDB): processed and harmonized the NASA fire data.
  • Machine learning (LightGBM, scikit-learn, SHAP): forecasts, fire-event grouping and explanations.
  • React, Vite, TypeScript: fast, responsive web interface.
  • Leaflet, Apache ECharts: interactive map, heatmap and charts.
  • GitHub Actions, Vercel: daily automatic updates and website hosting.

Creativity

  • A full chain of satellite data, harmonized record, forecast, and decision.
  • Machine learning combined with transparent rules anyone can check.
  • Rescue priority shares limited teams across several critical fires.
  • Plain-language reasons and visible data freshness build trust.
  • Runs automatically at no cost, so it can stay online after the hackathon.

Benefits

For agencies and communities:

  • One consistent fire picture across three countries.
  • Early, explainable warnings with clear actions.
  • Rescue teams sent where risk is highest.

For the environment:

  • Earlier action on carbon-rich peat fires.
  • Less transboundary haze and its health effects.
  • Better prevention planning by district and season.

Limitations

  • Clouds and smoke can hide fires from satellites.
  • Some inputs, such as peat depth and population, use simplified values.
  • Recommendations follow predefined rules.
  • Notifications run in Telegram demo mode.
  • Covers Borneo only.

Future Improvements

  • AI-generated recommendations based on live resources.
  • SMS and email alerts, plus agency feedback.
  • Burned-area mapping and more frequent updates.
  • Real-world pilots with agencies in Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia.
